title: Squarified two-level treemap of library loans with merge rules
prompt:
Build a two-level treemap of 2025 loans at Northgate Public Library as one SVG with viewBox 0 0 1200 800, from loans_2025.json (six departments, each with a color and its collections with 2025 and 2024 loans).

Title 'Where Northgate’s loans went in 2025', subtitle 'Area proportional to loans · <total> loans in total' with the grand total of 2025 loans written with thousands separators, and footer 'Source: Northgate Public Library circulation export'.

Data rules:
- Leave out collections with no 2025 loans.
- Inside each department, collections with less than 3% of that department’s 2025 loans are combined into one tile named 'Other' (2025 and 2024 loans summed), which then takes its place in the size order like any other tile. If only one collection in a department is that small, it keeps its own tile.

Layout (exact; coordinates will be checked in the source):
- The treemap fills the rectangle from (40, 120) to (1160, 760). Both levels use the squarified layout: sort items by 2025 loans, largest first; fill a strip along the shorter side of the remaining rectangle, adding the next item to the strip as long as that does not make the worst aspect ratio in the strip worse; then fix the strip and continue with the rest. When the remaining rectangle is at least as wide as it is tall, the strip is a column at its left edge filled top to bottom; otherwise it is a row along its top edge filled left to right. Areas are exactly proportional to loans.
- Each department rectangle is filled with the department color. Its collections are laid out inside it, inset 4 units on the left, right and bottom and 26 units at the top (the header band). Draw each collection tile inset 1 unit on every side of its computed rectangle.
- Header band text: '<department> · <total>k · <share>%' (2025 total in thousands and share of all loans, one decimal each) in 14-unit bold white Inter, 8 units from the department’s left edge. If that does not fit in the department width minus 16, show only the department name; if the name does not fit either, leave the band empty.

Tiles:
- Fill by change against 2024: above +5% the department color; from −5% to +5% the color mixed 55% with 45% white; below −5% the color mixed 25% with 75% white. Tile text is white on the full color and #1f2937 on the two tints.
- Label a tile only when its drawn size is at least 80 by 36: the collection name in 12-unit semibold (wrapped onto a second line if needed) and below it the loans in thousands with one decimal, like '98.4k', all inside the tile. Smaller tiles get no text.
- Every tile has a data-name attribute with its collection name and a title child like 'General fiction: 98,400 loans (+3.5% vs 2024)'.

Add a legend for the three change bands, and give each department group the id dept-<department id>.

rubric.criterion: Department rectangles are exact (x, y, width, height within 1.5 units; check the source): Fiction (40, 120, 329.4, 640.0); Children & Teens (369.4, 120, 535.3, 348.9); Digital (369.4, 468.9, 535.3, 291.1); Non-fiction (904.8, 120, 255.2, 418.0); Audio & Video (904.8, 538.0, 194.4, 222.0); Local History (1099.1, 538.0, 60.9, 222.0).

Fiction's seven tiles follow the squarified rule (computed rectangles x, y, w, h within 1.5 units; the drawn tiles are these inset by 1): General fiction (44.0, 146.0, 321.4, 196.3); Crime & thriller (44.0, 342.3, 197.7, 231.1); Science fiction & fantasy (241.7, 342.3, 123.7, 231.1); Romance (44.0, 573.4, 136.6, 182.6); Historical fiction (180.6, 573.4, 140.2, 101.3); Graphic novels (180.6, 674.6, 140.2, 81.4); Other (320.8, 573.4, 44.6, 182.6).

Merge rules: Fiction has an 'Other' tile of 12,710 loans (Short stories, Poetry and Plays) and Non-fiction an 'Other' tile of 8,650 (Computing, Languages, Religion & philosophy); Comics for kids keeps its own tile in Children & Teens (the only small collection there); there is no Microfilm tile; no other department has an Other tile and no merged collection also appears on its own.

Change tints are right: full color for Picture books (+5.1%), Graphic novels, E-audiobooks and Vinyl; the 55% tint for General fiction (+3.5%), Cookery, E-magazines and Fiction's Other (−3.0%); the 25% tint for History (−5.02%, just below −5%), Romance (−5.6%), DVDs & Blu-ray, Business & money and Non-fiction's Other (−8.0%). Text is white on full-color tiles and dark on the tints.

Label rule: tiles drawn at least 80 by 36 show name and value (e.g. General fiction '98.4k', Audiobooks on CD '11.3k' kept inside its 96-wide tile, Non-fiction's Other '8.7k'); smaller tiles have no text: Fiction's Other, Comics for kids, Streaming film, Arts & crafts, Business & money, Video games, Music CDs, Vinyl and all four Local History tiles. No label spills outside its tile.

Header bands read 'Fiction · 305.8k · 29.4%', 'Children & Teens · 270.9k · 26.1%', 'Digital · 226.0k · 21.7%' and 'Non-fiction · 154.8k · 14.9%'; Audio & Video shows only its name; the Local History band is empty.

Title 'Where Northgate’s loans went in 2025', subtitle 'Area proportional to loans · 1,039,710 loans in total' and footer 'Source: Northgate Public Library circulation export' are exact, and a legend explains the three change bands.

File quality: every tile has data-name and a title child in the given format (e.g. 'General fiction: 98,400 loans (+3.5% vs 2024)', 'Crime & thriller: 71,250 loans (+10.0% vs 2024)'); department groups are dept-fiction, dept-children, dept-digital, dept-non-fiction, dept-audio-video and dept-local-history.
Professional result: 2-unit gaps between tiles, department colors from the file, one consistent type scale, readable text contrast on every labeled tile, and nothing outside the viewBox.

title: Directed chord diagram of interregional moves with exact arcs
prompt:
Make a chord diagram of 2025 moves between the seven regions of Estavia as one SVG with viewBox 0 0 1200 900, from moves_2025.json (regions with colors, and moves as from, to and people, listed in no particular order).

Title 'Who moved where in Estavia, 2025' and subtitle 'Moves between regions: <n> people · plus <m> moves within a region, not shown', with both totals computed from the file and written with thousands separators. Footer 'Source: Estavia civil registry'.

Geometry (exact; the source will be checked):
- Centre (440, 470). Region arcs are ring segments between radius 300 and 318, in the order of the regions list, clockwise, the first starting exactly at 12 o'clock. Each region’s arc angle is proportional to its outflow (people who left it for another region), and every arc is followed by a 2° gap, so the arcs share 346°.
- Moves within a region are left out entirely: not in the arcs, not drawn.
- One ribbon per pair of regions with any moves between them. At region A’s end the ribbon is as wide as the moves from A to B; at B’s end, as wide as those from B to A. Within each arc the ribbon ends are laid out clockwise in the order of the regions list. Ribbon ends are arcs of radius 296 and the sides are quadratic Bézier curves with their control point at the centre.
- Color each ribbon with the region that sends more people in that pair, at 70% opacity, and draw the ribbons from the largest total (both directions) to the smallest, so small ribbons stay on top.
- Ticks outside each arc every 5,000 people counted from its start, labeled '0' at the start and then every 10,000 as '10k', '20k', and so on.
- Region names outside the ticks, following the circle with textPath and reading upright (never upside down) on the lower half.

Right-hand panel (from x 850):
- 'Net migration': a diverging bar chart of each region’s inflow minus outflow, sorted from most positive to most negative, 12 units of bar length per 1,000 people, labeled like '+1,234' and '−1,234'.
- 'Largest flows': the five largest single directions, largest first, like 'Northreach → Westerly 900'.

Give each arc the id arc-<region id> and each ribbon the id ribbon-<a>-<b> (a before b in the regions list), and keep all text as real text.

rubric.criterion: Arc angles are exact (within 0.5°, clockwise from 12 o'clock): Northreach 0.00–43.03°, Portmere 45.03–132.84°, Eastfen 134.84–181.17°, Highvale 183.17–219.03°, Saltcoast 221.03–263.28°, Midmoor 265.28–329.44°, Westerly 331.44–358.00°. (Counting within-region moves would change every angle.) E.g. Portmere's outer edge runs from about (665.0, 245.3) to (673.2, 686.2).

Exactly 20 ribbons: every pair except Eastfen–Westerly (no moves either way). Ribbon ends are right (within 0.5°): Portmere–Midmoor spans 98.72–122.95° at Portmere (12,500) and 275.56–304.25° at Midmoor (14,800); Northreach–Portmere spans 0.00–15.89° at Northreach and 45.03–57.44° at Portmere; Midmoor–Westerly spans 320.92–329.44° at Midmoor and 350.83–358.00° at Westerly.

Ribbon shape and order: ends are arcs of radius 296 and the sides are quadratic curves with control point (440, 470); ribbons are drawn largest total first (Portmere–Midmoor first, Highvale–Saltcoast last).

Ribbon colors follow the larger sender, at 70% opacity: Portmere–Midmoor and Midmoor–Westerly in Midmoor's color; Portmere–Eastfen and Eastfen–Highvale in Eastfen's; Northreach–Highvale and Highvale–Westerly in Highvale's; Portmere–Westerly in Portmere's; Portmere–Saltcoast in Saltcoast's.

The subtitle reads exactly 'Moves between regions: 178,500 people · plus 116,100 moves within a region, not shown'; the title 'Who moved where in Estavia, 2025' and footer 'Source: Estavia civil registry' are exact.
Ticks every 5,000 people from each arc start (39 in total, e.g. 10 on Portmere and 3 on Westerly), labeled '0' at each start and '10k', '20k', … every 10,000 (Portmere up to '40k').
Region names follow the circle outside the ticks using textPath and all read upright: Eastfen, Highvale and Saltcoast on the lower half are not upside down.

Net migration bars, sorted: Portmere +7,800, Westerly +2,600, Midmoor −400, Eastfen −1,600, Northreach −2,000, Saltcoast −3,000, Highvale −3,400, diverging from one zero line at 12 units per 1,000 (Portmere 93.6 long, Highvale 40.8).
Largest flows, in order: Midmoor → Portmere 14,800; Portmere → Midmoor 12,500; Eastfen → Portmere 11,200; Portmere → Eastfen 9,800; Saltcoast → Portmere 9,400.

File quality and layout: ids arc-northreach … arc-westerly and ribbon ids like ribbon-portmere-midmoor (a before b in list order); text as text elements; tick labels, names and the panel never collide, and everything fits inside the viewBox.
Polished result: the file's region colors used consistently on arcs, ribbons and bars, a clear hierarchy, readable small labels and no clutter.

title: Octilinear transit map with shared corridors and bend rules
prompt:
Draw the network map of Kestrel City Rail as one SVG with viewBox 0 0 1200 860, from network.json: 23 stations on a grid, four lines with their station order and color, and the River Kess as a polyline in grid units.

Rules (the geometry will be checked in the source):
- A station at grid (gx, gy) sits at x = 60 + 40 × gx, y = 120 + 40 × gy. The river points use the same mapping.
- Track between consecutive stations of a line is one straight segment when they are level, directly above each other, or exactly diagonal (45°). Otherwise it is two straight segments: leave the earlier station of the pair (in the line’s order) at 45° until level with or directly above or below the later one, then run straight into it. Bends may be rounded with a radius of at most 12. No other angles anywhere.
- Lines are 6-unit strokes in their colors with round caps. Where two lines serve the same consecutive stations, draw them side by side 8 units apart centre to centre, centred on the track, never crossing or overlapping inside the shared stretch.
- Stations: a stop served by one line is a short tick in the line color; an interchange (served by two or more lines) is a white circle or capsule with a 2.5-unit black outline covering all its strokes. The closed station (closed: true) keeps a tick but in gray, and its label is gray italic with ' (closed)' added.
- Every station is labeled horizontally in 12-unit Inter, the termini of each line in bold 13. No label may touch a line, a station symbol or another label. Airport gets a small plane pictogram next to its name.
- The river is a 16-unit pale blue band behind everything, with 'River Kess' in italic running along it (textPath).

Right of the map: the title 'Kestrel City Rail', the subtitle 'Network map · Autumn 2026 · not to scale', and a legend with one row per line in file order (color swatch, then '<line name> · <n> stations · <first> – <last>') plus the interchange and closed-station symbols.

Group each line as g id line-<line id> and each station as g id st-<station id>.

rubric.criterion: Stations sit on the grid mapping (symbol centres within 5 units, allowing for parallel strokes): e.g. Central (500, 440), Airport (900, 240), Brookside (620, 760), Elm Park (140, 200), Kilnworth (180, 640), Harbour Point (860, 520).

The bend rule is followed (check the source; points within 5 units to allow for parallel offsets): Docklands to Airport runs diagonally from (740, 440) to (900, 280), then straight up to (900, 240); Docklands to Harbour Point diagonally to (820, 520), then right to (860, 520); Northgate to University diagonally from (460, 280) to (500, 320), then down; Beacon Hill to University diagonally from (340, 320) to (380, 360), then right; Millbrook to Tanner Row diagonally from (180, 480) to (220, 440), then right; Canal Street to Southmead diagonally from (420, 600) to (380, 640), then left.
Octilinear only: every track segment is horizontal, vertical or at 45° (rounded bends of radius 12 or less allowed); no curves between stations and no other angles.

Shared stretches are parallel strokes 8 units apart that never cross or overlap: Harbour Line and Airport Express from Market Square through Central and Riverside to Docklands; Crown Line and Garden Line from University through Central to Old Town.

Interchange symbols (white, black outline, covering all strokes) at exactly Market Square, Central, Riverside, Docklands, University and Old Town; every other station has a tick in its line color; Abbotsford's tick is gray and its label reads 'Abbotsford (closed)' in gray italic.

All 23 stations are labeled with exact names, horizontally, and no label touches a line, a station symbol or another label (check around Central, University and Old Town); the termini Crown Heights, Brookside, Westgate, Harbour Point, Elm Park, Kilnworth, Market Square and Airport are bold; Airport has a plane pictogram.
The River Kess is a pale blue band through (60, 540), (400, 540), (480, 620) and (920, 620), behind the lines, with 'River Kess' in italic along it using textPath.

Legend rows in file order read exactly 'Crown Line · 9 stations · Crown Heights – Brookside', 'Harbour Line · 8 stations · Westgate – Harbour Point', 'Garden Line · 9 stations · Elm Park – Kilnworth' and 'Airport Express · 5 stations · Market Square – Airport', with interchange and closed symbols; title 'Kestrel City Rail' and subtitle 'Network map · Autumn 2026 · not to scale'.
File quality: groups line-crown, line-harbour, line-garden and line-airport, and st-<id> groups for all 23 stations; labels are text elements.

title: Horizontal sundial dial for Porto with computed hour lines

- The gnomon is a 10-unit-thick plate on the noon line; seen from above it is the rectangle from x 475 to 485, y 270 to 600. Morning hour lines radiate from its west root (475, 600) and afternoon lines from its east root (485, 600); the noon line rises from both.
- The hour line for hour h (6 to 18, local solar time) makes the angle θ = atan(sin 41.15° × tan(15° × (h − 12))) with the noon line, to the west before noon and to the east after it; 6 and 18 run due west and due east. Each hour line is exactly 340 units long from its root.
- Half-hour marks run from 310 to 340 units along their own lines and quarter-hour marks from 325 to 340, from the same roots (same formula with fractional h).
- The chapter ring is a pair of concentric semicircles of radius 300 and 340 around (480, 600), above the root line.
- Hour numerals VI VII VIII IX X XI XII I II III IV V VI, upright, centred 375 units from the root along their hour line (VI at both ends).
- The dial plate is a circle of radius 440 around (480, 520), filled like polished brass, with a double engraved border. Along its lower rim the motto 'LUX UMBRA DEI · TEMPUS FUGIT' follows the edge (textPath), and below the root sits a small compass rose with N pointing up.

- 'Gnomon elevation': a right triangle with a horizontal base from (980, 400) to (1140, 400) whose style rises from (980, 400) at exactly 41.15° to the vertical side at x 1140; mark the angle with an arc labeled '41.15°' and put S under the left end and N under the right end.
- A table 'Hour-line angles' listing 1 h to 6 h from noon with θ to one decimal, like '1 h · 10.0°'.
- A note giving the correction from sundial time to UTC (4 minutes of time per degree of longitude, rounded to the whole second) in the form 'Add <m> min <s> s to sundial time for UTC'.
- The title 'PORTO', the line '41.15° N · 8.61° W' and one short sentence saying that the dial shows local solar time.

rubric.criterion: Hour-line angles are exact: in the source the lines end (340 from their roots, within 2 units) at IX (288.1, 316.0), X (354.2, 282.2), XI (416.0, 265.2), I (544.0, 265.2), III (671.9, 316.0) and V (799.9, 471.8), and the VI lines end at (135, 600) and (825, 600).

Half- and quarter-hour marks use the same formula and roots: the 9:30 mark ends at (321.8, 296.5), 2:30 at (638.2, 296.5), 11:45 at (460.3, 260.3) and 12:15 at (499.7, 260.3) (within 2 units); half marks are 30 long, quarter marks 15.

Numerals VI … XII … VI are upright and centred 375 from their roots along their lines within 4 units: IX at (268.9, 286.7), III at (691.1, 286.7), XII near (480, 225), and VI at (100, 600) and (860, 600).

Chapter ring of two semicircles (radius 300 and 340 around (480, 600)) above the root line; the plate is a circle of radius 440 around (480, 520) with a brass-like gradient and a double border; a compass rose with N up sits below the root.
The motto 'LUX UMBRA DEI · TEMPUS FUGIT' follows the lower rim using textPath and reads upright, left to right.
Gnomon elevation: base (980, 400)–(1140, 400) and the vertical side at x 1140 reaching (1140, 260.2) within 1.5 units (a 41.15° style), with an angle arc labeled '41.15°' and S and N under the ends.

title: SMIL bar chart race of metro station entries

Use SMIL only (animate, set, animateTransform), with no CSS animation and no script, so it can be scrubbed with setCurrentTime. Data: entries.csv (millions of entries per station and year, with each station’s line and line color; an empty cell means the station was not open yet: treat it as 0 and rank it below every open station).

Timeline:
- One cycle lasts 16 s and repeats forever. Year 2018 + k (k = 0 to 7) is shown exactly at t = 2k s; between two keyframes every bar moves and grows linearly; from 14 s to 16 s the chart holds 2025, then it restarts at 2018.
- Ranking in each year: by value, largest first; equal values rank alphabetically.

Chart:
- The top 8 of each year are visible. A bar with rank r (1 to 8) has its top at y = 140 + 72 × (r − 1) and a height of 56; bars ranked 9 or lower sit at y = 716, hidden by a clip of the bar area that ends at y = 708, so bars slide in and out at the bottom.

Title 'Busiest stations on Kestrel Metro', subtitle 'Annual entries in millions, 2018–2025 · top 8 each year', and a small legend of the four lines. Give each station’s bar group the id bar-<station name in lowercase with hyphens>.

rubric.criterion: SMIL only: no script, no CSS @keyframes or animation properties; all animations begin at 0 with a 16 s cycle (dur 16s, or equivalent) and repeatCount indefinite, so they stay in sync. To check timing, open the SVG directly in a browser page and scrub it with pauseAnimations() and setCurrentTime(t).

Keyframe ranks: at t = 0 the order is Central, Market Square, University, Riverside, Old Town, Northgate, Airport, Docklands; at t = 6 (2021) Central, Market Square, Riverside, University (tied at 38.4, broken alphabetically), Old Town, Docklands, Northgate, Beacon Hill; at t = 14 (2025) Central, Market Square, University, Docklands, Harbour Gate, Riverside, Old Town, Airport.

Labels: the year label shows 2019 at t = 3, 2021 at t = 6.5 and 2025 at t = 15; value labels switch at the keyframes (Central shows '90.1M' at t = 3 and '49.6M' at t = 4.5) and ride along with the bar ends.
Clip: bars ranked 9 or lower are invisible below y 708 at keyframes, and bars never cover the axis labels or the title.

Static parts: title 'Busiest stations on Kestrel Metro', subtitle 'Annual entries in millions, 2018–2025 · top 8 each year', axis 0–100 with gridlines every 20, and a legend of Crown, Harbour, Garden and Airport Express with their colors.
File quality: groups bar-central, bar-market-square, …, bar-harbour-gate and bar-tanner-row for all 12 stations; names right-aligned at x 250; values formatted like '88.4M'.
Smooth and legible race: consistent bar colors by line, no label collisions at keyframes, and a clear, large year label.

title: Stereographic star chart with a projected ecliptic
prompt:
Make a star chart of the northern sky as one SVG with viewBox 0 0 1200 1000, from stars.csv (101 stars with right ascension in hours, declination in degrees, magnitude and constellation) and figures.json (the stick figure of each constellation as pairs of star names).

Projection (exact; positions will be checked in the source):
- Polar stereographic around the north celestial pole, centred at (500, 500): a star at declination δ lies at radius r = k × tan((90° − δ) / 2), with k chosen so that δ = −30° falls exactly on r = 440, the edge of the chart.
- Right ascension α (in hours) sets the direction: x = 500 + r × sin(15° × α), y = 500 + r × cos(15° × α), so 0h points straight down and 6h to the right.

Content:
- A dark sky disc of radius 440 with a thin rim; declination circles at +60°, +30° and 0° (the celestial equator, slightly stronger); hour lines every 2h from the +60° circle to the rim; labels 0h to 23h just outside the rim and +60°, +30° and 0° along the 0h line.
- The ecliptic (obliquity 23.44°) as a dashed gold curve computed through the projection.
- Stars as white discs sized by magnitude: below 0.5 radius 7; from 0.5 to below 1.5 radius 5.5; from 1.5 to below 2.5 radius 4; from 2.5 to below 3.5 radius 2.8; 3.5 and fainter radius 1.8.

A task of d days occupies d consecutive working days. A milestone (0 days) happens at the end of the day its last predecessor finishes.
- Compute total float (latest minus earliest start, in working days) with a backward pass from the project finish; the tasks with zero float form the critical path.
